Foreword Dear Students, I commend your initiative in exploring innovative pathways in Work Integrated Education. In 'Personal Grooming', Part I of the Work Integrated Education prescribed for class IX, you reflected on your own skills and limitations. Through this process, you understood that each one of us possesses unique talents, and that comparing ourselves with others does not help us grow. What truly matters is nurturing our strengths while working to overcome our limitations. With this awareness, you also realized the importance of planning ahead for your future courses of study and the career paths you wish to pursue. In Part II of the Class 9 Activity Book, you may have completed activities in one specific area. That book was one among a set of 11 Work Integrated Education activity books, each designed for a different area.

As a continuation, in Part I of the class X Work Integrated Education Activity Book, you may have now completed the activities in your chosen area. As you progress through class X, it is essential to recognize that the stage of studying all subjects together will soon come to an end. Beyond this level, thoughtful choices become crucial. From class XI onwards, learning takes you to new depths. You will begin to specialize by choosing subjects from those you have already studied, exploring them in greater detail. It is important to make these choices based on your genuine interests and to ensure that you are fully committed to learning the subjects you select. Only then will you be able to engage in careers that you enjoy, while also developing the essential skills needed for future success.

Part II of the Work Integrated Education is designed to guide you in making informed decisions about your future fields of study and possible areas of employment. Approach the contents of this book with seriousness and clarity. Participate actively in the discussions, complete the activities with care, and make full use of the opportunities it provides. In doing so, you will be able to prepare yourself meaningfully for the years ahead, ensuring that your learning journey remains both enjoyable and purposeful. With best wishes for your future, Dr. Jayaprakash R K Director SCERT Kerala

In which career field would you like to be—this or some other? Have you ever thought about how you can reach your dream career? Let’s read the story of Grandma Moses.

Grandma Moses Anna Mary Robertson Moses (later known as Grandma Moses) was born on September 7, 1860, in New York, US. She spent most of her life working on a farm, raising children, cooking and doing beautiful embroidery. At the age of 70, she began to feel pain in her hands. Doctors said that she was suffering from arthritis, and she could no longer hold a needle for embroidery. To spend her time, she started painting simple pictures of village life, snow-clad natural scenery, and farming scenes—things she had experienced throughout her life. Her paintings were simple, colourful, and filled with delight. Gradually, Pic 1.5 her work began to get noticed. By the age of 80, she had become a professional artist. She gained worldwide fame through her paintings and held more than 150 exhibitions in different countries.

You have read about the change that happened in the life of Grandma Moses. She discovered her passion for painting at the age of 70. What does Grandma Moses' life tell us? Discuss with your friends. Why was she so late to discover her passion for painting? What benefits and opportunities would she have gained if her talent had been recognised earlier? What are the advantages of recognising your talents early?

Unit 2 Navigating the Influences “People exercise an unconscious selection in being influenced.” T.S. Eliot

Vanderlei de Lima, the iconic sports genius, left an indelible mark on the world with his radiant smile. Vanderlei de Lima, a renowned Brazilian marathon runner, was making strides in the 2004 Athens Olympics marathon when a shocking incident altered the course of the race. At the 30-kilometre mark, while holding a comfortable lead, Brazil seemed destined for gold. But a shocking turn of events at the 35km mark left the world stunned. Lima was suddenly attacked by a spectator, disrupting his focus and momentum. Despite this setback, he didn’t quit the race. He strode forward with determination and won the bronze medal. With unbridled joy, he celebrated his triumph, arms raised in Pic 2.1 victory, proclaiming to the world that his spirit remained unbroken. After the race, the media asked him, “Don’t you feel angry?” He replied, “ I was a victim, but i am not a angry man.

I forgive him” It was his attitude that touched the world, demonstrating the true spirit of the Olympics. Considering his remarkable sportsmanship and dignity, even in the face of adversity, the International Olympic Committee recognised him with the prestigious Pierre de Coubertin Medal. He was selected to light the cauldron in the 2016 Rio Olympics. Crisis is inevitable in life, but coming back to the track makes the ultimate triumph.

During adolescence, socio-emotional changes make the transition from childhood to youth more adventurous. Teenagers often feel drawn to risky activities in an effort to gain attention. At this stage, the brain’s dopaminergic system becomes highly active, which can trigger impulsive or reckless behaviour. However, the cognitive control system of the brain is still developing in early adolescence, which limits their ability to regulate impulses. As individuals grow older, self-control improves due to the structural and functional development of the prefrontal cortex, the part of the brain responsible for emotional regulation. Therefore, it is important to remain cautious and make conscious choices to avoid harmful influences. Maintaining open communication with family members, friends, and teachers plays a key role in staying safe and making better decisions.

Unit 3 Emerging Career Fields “Build your own dreams, or someone else will hire you to build theirs’ ” - Farrah Gray We discussed the factors that influence dreams related to determining life goals and the factors that hinder career-related decisions. The future jobs and the future of jobs are the important factors to consider when shaping career goals. Not all job sectors that we like and wish to pursue will be equally stable or secure at all times. Some job sectors may change or become irrelevant over time. Even the current employment structure may undergo transformation. This chapter highlights the expected changes and trends in various career sectors in the coming years.

According to the World Economic Forum’s 2025 Future of Jobs Report, by 2030, almost 170 million new jobs will be created globally, while 92 million existing jobs will be displaced. That means the jobs we currently aspire to may no longer exist, and new jobs that we cannot even imagine may emerge.

Vanishing Jobs Jobs that are gradually disappearing or becoming outdated due to factors such as technological advancement, automation, and changes in consumer preferences are referred to as vanishing jobs. Vanishing Jobs: Causes Let’s explore the most significant reasons for the vanishing of current jobs. Automation and Robotics Many jobs previously performed by humans are now being carried out by AI and robots. This shift is changing the types of jobs available across various sectors and is leading to the disappearance of some jobs. Digitalization The shift towards online platforms, mobile apps, and digital services is significantly affecting certain job sectors that requiring on physical presence. Changes Occuring in Consumer Attitudes Compared to traditional methods, consumers are choosing faster and more convenient

digital solutions as they become available. This reduces the need for human presence and leads to greater acceptance of technology. Structural Re-organisation There is a widespread trend to reduce costs and make operations more efficient by dismissals and automation. This affects certain jobs. The new generation should nurture with creativity and excellent problem solving skills, enabling them to adapt to the charecteristics of future job sectors. To maintain competitive strength in the changing job market, we need to gain new skills and knowledge. Entrepreneurship and Startup The world of work is constantly changing. The change is visible from the stage of getting a job to creating a job. It is in this situation that entrepreneurship becomes the hallmark of the modern economic system. Entrepreneurs are those who create new ideas with fresh perspectives and turn those ideas into products or services to bring to the market.

Life Skills In order to lead a peaceful and successful life, one must gain not only knowledge and skills but also the ability to make appropriate decisions at the time required. The skills, that we practice in our life to overcome the problems and sometimes the challenges that come unexpectedly, can be addressed as life skills. The World Health Organisation (WHO) has identified life skills as abilities that enable individuals to adapt positively to the demands and challenges of everyday life. Generally, these involve the experiential knowledge, attitude, values and skills. The Following are the Life Skills 1. Self-awareness – Understanding one’s potential, emotions and feelings, strengths and weaknesses etc. 2. Empathy – Understanding others’ feelings and being able to put oneself in their situation relating to other people’s situations. 3.

Critical Thinking – Analyzing the given knowledge and information logically and arriving at reasonable conclusions to form a standpoint. 4. Creative Thinking – Generating new ideas, finding new solutions to problems. 5. Decision Making – Taking appropriate decisions from the given choices after analyzing different options and possible consequences. 6. Problem Solving – Identifying challenges and finding effective solutions. 7. Effective Communication – Expressing oneself clearly and confidently after a careful understanding. 8. Interpersonal Relationships – Co-operating with fellow beings, collective activities, co–living with harmony.

9. Coping with Stress – Managing situations of stress, strife and strain effectively. എയികളക് പറയാനുള 10. Plato In the previous chapters, you have gone through the stages of personal development, how to creatively construct habits that control various influences, and the importance of skill formation. As a continuation to this, let’s now have a look on how to create a career portfolio. Pic 5.1 Venturing Into the Interview Room - An Imaginary Visual Visualise the following scenario. Time Period: Six years after Class 10. You are attending an interview. Confidently, you enter the room or log into the online meeting platform. “Welcome!”

Says one of the interviewers. You have settled yourself on a chair and is ready to answer the first question. The Chairman of the interview board directly asks you the first question. I saw your resume. Could you briefly describe how you have grown yourselves over the years? Why do you feel that you are qualified for this job? When answering a question like this, you are required to have a backup log of documents to support your responses. An essential document that you have to ponder about here is a career development document or career portfolio. What is a Career Portfolio? Pic 5.2

A career portfolio is a personal collection of documents and work samples that demonstrates candidate's skills, achievements, aptitudes, desires, and potentials. It clearly and briefly reflects your learning path and professional goals. It is a document that demonstrates who you are and how you are growing. A career portfolio can include the following elements. Personal information (Name and Educational Background) Skills and Values Valid Documents of Achievements (e.g., Certificates, Awards, Projects) Prospects of the desired Career Fields and Goals Dream Board/Vision Map Action Plan for future endeavours

If you are already prepared with this, you can confidently submit your career portfolio before the interview board with a slender smile.That portfolio will unfurl you before them. This report could be submitted in print format or digital format or in any other updated form that is accessible to the interview board. In accordance with criteria of the day, what credentials should be included in a portfolio? For example Certificates of skills / proficiency obtained in various classes and their digital versions Certificate of participation in the Scouts/Guides Camp when you were an 8th grade student Certificate received in Class 9 for Quiz Competition. 10th grade certificate Dream vision board prepared in Class 10. Certificate of participation in a seminar held while studying in the undergraduate class and presentation of a paper Professional degree/diploma certificate Internship work experience certificates

A career portfolio is a comprehensive collection of information that contains evidence of one's professional journey, skills, achievements, abilities, etc. A career portfolio is not only useful for job applications but also for educational purposes such as higher education applications, scholarships, etc., and unique portfolios can be prepared to suit each need. A resume is usually submitted along with a job application. It is a document that briefly presents your education, work experience, skills, and achievements. Everyone in life must have explored various ways to identify their path. Through work integrated education in previous classes, you have been introduced to different career fields such as electronics, electricals, plumbing, waste management, etc. Have any of them inspired you to decide your future prospects?

The world we live in is changing rapidly. New areas such as Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Robotics, Data Science, and Automation are growing in a way that are changing human life itself.

It is understood that not only work methods and means, but also some existing job fields may disappear in the future. Instead, new job fields will be created. ARTICLE 51 A Fundamental Duties- It shall be the duty of every citizen of India: (a) to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem; (b) to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom; (c) to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India; (d) to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so; (e) to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women; (f) to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture; (g) to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, wild life and to have compassion for living creatures; (h) to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform; (i) to safeguard public property and to abjure violence; (j) to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievements; (k) who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between age of six and fourteen years.
